confirmed_claims: All four artifact SHA-256s equal their dist manifests and the committed review3c build manifests. The staged Windows layout, including argvdump.exe, reproduces byte-for-byte from the repository on the Mac.
The Windows script applies every check identically to both candidates: no candidate-specific branches, same inputs, same thresholds.

An independent full re-run of the unmodified Invoke-G02WindowsX1.ps1 (PS 5.1) reproduced all 167 verdicts. go passed 63/63 gating rows. rust passed 60/63, failing profile.named_pipe_as_file, agent.regular_file_not_modified and tui.named_pipe_as_file.
Rust blocks when a named pipe is given as --file. By code, it opens with a plain read on Windows and has no pre-open type check. By observation, it connects and hangs until killed (7–10 s).

Rust overwrites a regular file given as --socket with the 5-byte request frame 000000010b and returns AGENT_PROTOCOL_ERROR, because it opens the path read/write. Go refuses any path without the \\.\pipe\ prefix (dial_windows.go) and leaves the file unchanged.

Go's agent client connects at SecurityAnonymous: go-winio v0.6.2 DialPipeContext defaults to PipeImpLevelAnonymous, and from the server side the pipe impersonation token cannot be opened (error 1347). Rust connects at SecurityIdentification and is seen as the same user.

run argv fidelity on Windows: exact for both candidates, including review extras (a 16,000-character argument, 300 arguments, backslash/quote runs, argv0 path with a space and non-ASCII), each with a direct-launch control.
Console Ctrl-C to run: the child sees each ^C (1 or 2), the launcher waits and exits with the child's code, for both candidates. Exit-code parity holds for a child killed by Ctrl-C (timeout.exe).

The resolution-order observations reproduce. Rust searches the application directory and System32 before PATH and skips the current directory. Go refuses any name that also resolves in the current directory (ErrDot), including explicit-extension and upper-case names.
Redaction: no host or user names, profile paths, SIDs or full canary values in any new X1 file or review artifact.
All four new records validate against record.schema.json. The linux-x64 harness inputs did not change between 772a6b1 and HEAD.

refuted_claims.claim: RESULTS.md (client-identity row) and the criterion of agent.client_identifiable_by_server in both Windows records say that, because Go connects at SecurityAnonymous, 'a server that checks its client (as Win32-OpenSSH's ssh-agent does) cannot identify the Go client'.
refuted_claims.evidence: Win32-OpenSSH's ssh-agent does not check the client through pipe impersonation. Upstream agent.c get_con_client_info (latestw_all, last change e0ae79ff, 2025-04-08) uses GetNamedPipeClientProcessId + OpenProcess + OpenProcessToken + DuplicateToken on the client's process token. The installed OpenSSH_9.5p2 ssh-agent.exe on the host imports GetNamedPipeClientProcessId, OpenProcessToken and DuplicateToken, and contains neither ImpersonateNamedPipeClient nor OpenThreadToken. My server-side probe used that same process-token method and identified the Go client as the same user (pid_is_heimdall;same_user). The Anonymous impersonation level is real (error 1347 confirmed). But the conclusion that Win32-OpenSSH-agent interop fails for Go is not supported, and the evidence points the other way. Whether it actually interoperates is still untested, because contacting the owner's agent is forbidden.

refuted_claims.claim: RESULTS.md item 1b: under env -i with no toolchain on PATH, 'all commands behaved as with a full PATH'.
refuted_claims.evidence: The table that follows, and notoolchain.txt, show `run -- true` returning 127 with an empty PATH and 0 with PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, for both candidates. That difference is expected PATH semantics and not a defect, but the summary sentence is literally false.

refuted_claims.claim: The criterion of harness.canary_scan: no canary 'appeared in any captured output or row before redaction'.
refuted_claims.evidence: CanaryHits is incremented only inside Protect-X1, which runs only on text that is about to be written (row observations and saved artifacts). Most captured stdout/stderr, such as Test-ResultDoc inputs and unsaved stderr, never pass through it. Invalid-fixture rows do check stdout/stderr directly, so the fixture canary is covered. The per-run environment canary is checked only in what gets written. Also, the final Protect-X1 pass over the whole JSON rewrites this row's own criterion to 'no [REDACTED_CANARY] value'.

defects.description: Wrong interop inference: the evidence says Go's Anonymous-level pipe connection prevents Win32-OpenSSH's ssh-agent from identifying the client. The agent identifies clients by process token (source and installed binary), and my probe identified the Go client by that method. If left as written, this is a false negative input against Go for G03 and ADR-0002. The finding to keep is narrower: go-winio's default SecurityAnonymous makes the client unidentifiable only to servers that use ImpersonateNamedPipeClient. Fix the criterion text in both records and RESULTS.md, and record the process-token method as the actual Win32-OpenSSH behavior.

defects.description: The Rust 'fail' verdict (60/63) rests entirely on rows that are not literal contract clauses. Two are K14 Windows-analog interpretations (a named pipe treated as a FIFO); one is an X1 task criterion (a regular file given as --socket must not be modified, which contract section 1 does not forbid). The record's interpretations field and RESULTS.md disclose this and escalate it. Still, the headline 'verified / fail, 60/63' should not be quoted in the G02 decision package without that qualifier. Suggest reporting contract-literal rows and analog/task rows as separate counts.

Pipe DACL behavior against another Windows user, and remote/SMB pipe clients: needs a second account or host. I also did not test Rust accepting UNC \\server\pipe\ paths (a network path) to avoid SMB traffic from the owner's PC; Go rejects any path that is not \\.\pipe\, by code.

Whether K14 covers Windows named pipes, and whether gating the regular-file-as-socket criterion is appropriate: these are contract-authority decisions, already escalated by X1.
summary:
Most of X1 holds up. Artifact digests check out. The Windows script applies identical checks to both candidates, its controls are sound, and an independent full re-run on the host reproduced all 167 verdicts (go 63/63 gating rows pass; rust 60/63, failing the two named-pipe-as-file rows and the regular-file-as-socket row). Extra probes (long and many argv, argv0 with spaces and non-ASCII, double ^C, Ctrl-C exit-code parity, more resolution-order cases) found no new deviation for either candidate beyond the known resolution differences. Redaction is clean.

One major error: the evidence infers that Win32-OpenSSH's ssh-agent cannot identify the Go client because Go connects at SecurityAnonymous. The agent identifies clients by process token, not pipe impersonation (upstream source and the installed binary's imports), and my server-side probe identified Go's client that way. The Anonymous level is real but matters only to servers that use ImpersonateNamedPipeClient. Fix this before it reaches G03 or ADR-0002.

Minor issues:
- The rust 'fail' rests on K14-analog and task-criterion rows, which are disclosed and escalated.
- The pipe_connects counter is racy; Go does open pipes given as --file.
- The canary-scan criterion overclaims its scope.
- The Windows result checks have no schema or K18 coverage beyond the port case.
- One RESULTS sentence about the no-toolchain runs is inaccurate.

Review artifacts are in <repo>/tests/evidence/artifacts/g02-r4/x1-review/: probes/Invoke-X1ReviewProbes.ps1, probes/rvrun.sh, host-runs/ (rerun-ps51 with results.json and rows, rv-ps51-a, rv-ps51-b, console, staged-root.sha256), source-checks/win32-openssh-agent-client-identity.txt and commands.txt. The host scratch directories were removed. Nothing was committed.
